title: Recall: up the ramp and back
text:
Spaced recall · kinematics

≈ 4 min

Recall: up the ramp and back

A cart is pushed up a ramp, then rolls back down. Up the ramp is +.

When is it at its highest point? What is its acceleration at that moment?

Solve alone · compare as a group · then check.

Velocity vs. time

Velocity vs. time. Velocity (m/s) versus Time (s). The line crosses zero at the top.

The line crosses zero at the top.

Answer

Where v = 0: t = 3 ÷ 1 = **3 s**.

Still **−1 m/s²** — acceleration isn't zero at the top.

title: A diagram is a force inventory
text:
Explicit instruction

Target S5

A diagram is a force inventory

•Name the object or system boundary.

•Represent it with a dot or simple body outline.

•Draw one arrow for each actual external force, starting at the object.

•Label the force type and agent. Choose axes.

•Use relative arrow lengths when magnitudes are known or constrained.

title: Six rules
text:
FBD rules

≈ 20 min

Six rules

01Draw just the object — or a dot.

02One arrow for EACH force on the object.

03Arrows point in the force's direction.

04Arrow length ∝ force magnitude.

05Label each arrow: F_gravity, F_normal, F_friction…

06ONLY forces ON the object — not forces it exerts on others.

title: Components do not create extra interactions
text:
Explicit instruction

Target S5 Practice

Components do not create extra interactions

When resolving a force, replace it with its components in the equations.

A component diagram may use dashed guides. Do not count the original force and both components in the same sum.

For a ramp, weight still points vertically downward before decomposition.
